correctness.rationale: PASS: A neighborhood face is exactly a family of 2-subsets supported on ≤n-2 ground letters. The equivariant support-union and all-pairs closure maps give a homotopy equivalence to the Boolean rank-selected poset of subsets of sizes 2..n-2. This is the full induced subcomplex of the barycentric boundary of the (n-1)-simplex after deleting singleton and co-singleton vertices. The complementary induced 1-complex is precisely the crown graph and the barycentric positive-weight deformation retract is equivariant. Integral Alexander duality (ambient sphere orientation sign=sgn) gives the asserted degree shift and sign twist. The crown graph oriented incidence coboundary has image all row/column sums, one relation, primitive image and rank n²-3n+1. The standard universal coefficient theorem yields all prime reductions, and elementary cochain traces yield sgn(f²-3f+1). The n=4 discrete boundary is included.

evidence: General Boolean rank-selected Specht theorem covers this poset, and Nilakantan–Singh Theorem 1.3 covers all KG(2,k) neighborhood ranks.
broader_coverage.reasoning: These dominate broad abstract module/rank components, preventing any novelty claim for them; they do not supply the specific graph cochain presentation in inspected text. If the latter is proven as a routine standard Specht re-presentation elsewhere, O would change.

value.rationale: PASS with bounded scope: The explicit crown-graph cochain lattice and primitive row/column relations give a natural uniform combinatorial integer presentation of a classical rank-selected Boolean homology module, useful especially for modular actions and explicit calculations. Its contribution is a concrete equivariant Alexander-dual model, not the previously established rank, rational Specht decomposition, or abstract ribbon Specht module. This is more than merely retyping a known Betti number.

limitations: n>=4, ordinary open-neighborhood KG(n,2), not higher Kneser parameters or equivariant homotopy.
Abstract/rational module, ranks and general ribbon Specht results are already prior work and must not be reasserted as new.
